newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: TENNIS-MUSTER AND KAFELNIKOV WIN BUT KUERTEN CRASHES.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-MUSTER AND KAFELNIKOV WIN BUT KUERTEN CRASHES.

text.p: French Open champion Gustavo Kuerten crashed out of the $535,000 Generali Open on Wednesday while Thomas Muster and Yevgeny Kafelnikov breezed into the third round.
Top seed and world number five Muster delighted the home crowd with a 6-3 6-1 win over Spain's Carlos Costa in a match interrupted once due to rain.
Second-seeded Russian Kafelnikov eliminated Brazil's Fernando Meligeni 6-1 6-3 but Kuerten bowed out to unfancied Argentine Hernan Gumy, also 6-1 6-3.
The clay court tournament's third seed, Spaniard Alex Corretja, struggled but got past Argentina's Luca Arnold 6-2 6-7 6-4.
Defending champion Alberto Berasategui of Spain, the fifth seed, suffered a surprise upset when he was beaten 6-2 6-3 by young Austrian Stefan Koubek, ranked 171st in the world.
Muster and Kafelnikov, French Open champions in 1995 and 1996 respectively, were pleased with their performances.
"I am happy to have won my first match here in Kitzbuehel," said Muster, who was known as the king of clay court tennis after a series of victories in 1995 but has struggled this year.
Kafelnikov, who was forced to take a four-month break due to a broken finger earlier in the year, said: "I felt good and had a lot of power today, especially at the beginning."
The fourth-seeded Kuerten said his poor showing was not a result of a stomach muscle injury sustained in the third round in Stuttgart last week.

"The injury is not the reason why I lost. I had a chance of reversing things at 3-2 in the second set but just didn't manage it," said the Brazilian who has lost his opening matches at six tournaments this year.

When asked if his surprise French Open title had put too much pressure on him, Kuerten said: "No. Things are still the same, I win some matches and lose others. The only difference now is that more people want to see me play.
"Everyone wants to get into the top 20, the competition is tough. Once you're at the top it's difficult to stay there."
